name: Do I need permits for a custom kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need permits for a custom kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do I need permits for a custom kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most custom kitchen remodels in Los Angeles require permits when the work goes beyond cosmetic replacement. If the project includes relocating plumbing, adding circuits, changing lighting, moving walls, altering load-bearing structures, or modifying ventilation, permits are typically part of the process. Even when the design feels straightforward, older homes in neighborhoods like Pasadena, Glendale, or Burbank may trigger additional review because existing systems often need upgrading to meet current code. The permit process can affect both timeline and budget, so it should be discussed before finalizing drawings. A good design-build team will identify permit-sensitive items early and prepare the scope accordingly. Homeowners should also ask whether inspections are built into the schedule, since delays often happen when rough plumbing, electrical, or framing work needs reinspection. If a contractor suggests skipping permits for work that clearly changes systems or structure, that is a major warning sign.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are usually required if a custom kitchen remodel changes plumbing, electrical, mechanical systems, walls, or structural elements. Cosmetic updates may not need permits, but most true custom kitchen projects do because they involve layout changes, upgraded systems, or code-compliance work.
